compression_settings.write_topology: tar::Builder replay: 512-byte header write; payload in 8192-byte writes with a short final write; one padding write to the next 512 boundary, omitted when the payload is already aligned; 1024-byte trailer; GzEncoder::finish()

notes: POSITIVE RESULT. SUPERSEDES the conclusion of 2026-08-13-macos-inprocess-recompression-probe; that record is retained unchanged and its measurements are all reproduced here. Standalone in-process recompression of the exact tar reproduces the official .app.tar.gz byte-for-byte, with no cargo-tauri involvement. Measured on two independent official artifacts from the same controlled build. v1.0.1: entry-aware topology produced 4070756 bytes, BLAKE3 718c104bfdcc00aaa7b588519ad62c2719a182d8e7364c1daf260ed8fbf96f36, identical to the official artifact; the existing minisign signature over the official artifact verifies against the rebuild. v1.0.0: entry-aware topology produced 4070693 bytes, BLAKE3 b8ce5a9e36b8e00453735fae64bc9d803e1bd06becff3112abdd622df97a1a8b, identical to the official artifact. Negative controls on v1.0.1, same encoder and level: one-shot write_all of the whole tar produced 4070510 bytes differing at byte 47, reproducing the earlier probe's number exactly; uniform 8192-byte chunking of the whole tar produced 4070674 bytes, also differing at byte 47. So the earlier probe was right that the encoder was not the variable and right about its own recipe; it was wrong to generalise from a one-shot write, because tauri-bundler does not compress a tar -- it streams tar::Builder into GzEncoder, and the encoder sees the archive as writes whose boundaries are the tar's own structure. Mechanism confirmed by reading tauri-bundler 2.8.1 src/bundle/updater_bundle.rs create_tar/create_tar_from_src and tar 0.4.46 src/builder.rs append_file/append_dir_all/pad_zeroes, which the earlier probe explicitly recorded as unread. BACKEND IS LOAD-BEARING: flate2's default miniz_oxide backend produces 3936113 bytes for every topology tried (differing at byte 12) and can never match, reproducing the 3936113-byte control in 2026-08-13-macos-controlled-tar-layer. zlib-rs is required. zlib-rs 0.6.7 matches even though the installed cargo-tauri binary resolves 0.6.3, so the two agree on this input; that is an observation about these versions, not a stability guarantee. Enabling both flate2 backends simultaneously still matches, so cargo feature unification in a consumer's graph does not silently break the recipe. GNU long-name ('L'/'K') entries are handled from a reading of tar's prepare_header_path -- payload one byte longer than the header declares, written as two calls -- and are NOT exercised by any artifact here, so that branch is inferred, not measured. The recipe is never trusted: its output is gated by the published installer digest and a mismatch falls back to a full download.
